security_spec.violation_condition: In QEMU, when software writes a reserved MODE value (≥2) to stvec or vstvec, the write_stvec/write_vstvec handlers at target/riscv/csr.c:4157-4166 and 5219-5228 silently drop the entire CSR write (both MODE and BASE fields) rather than implementing WARL behavior that legalizes MODE while preserving BASE. The spec now explicitly requires STVEC_MODE_WARL and STVEC_BASE_WARL with impl-def-behavior. The silent-drop pattern means the guest kernel's attempt to update the trap vector base address is entirely lost when MODE is reserved — the BASE update is incorrectly discarded along with the illegal MODE, rather than the BASE being WARL-preserved and MODE being WARL-mapped to a legal value (e.g., Direct=0). Additionally, the RAW write to mnepc at line 5474 performs no alignment masking for bit 0 or IALIGN-dependent bit 1, violating the MNEPC_WARL normative rule that mnepc[0] must always read zero and mnepc[1:0] must read zero when IALIGN=32.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: CSR write handler that silently ignores entire register write on partial illegal-field instead of per-field WARL legalization; raw unchecked CSR assignment without WARL bit masking on epc-style registers
security_spec.summary: QEMU silently drops full stvec/vstvec writes on reserved MODE instead of per-field WARL legalization, and applies no WARL masking to mnepc/mncause/mnstatus — the newly formalized WARL normative rules (STVEC_MODE_WARL, STVEC_BASE_WARL, MNEPC_WARL, MNCAUSE_WARL, MNSTATUS_WARL) are either unimplemented or incorrectly implemented as silent-write-drop
